narrative.overview: nelody seq watches a melody walk. The Tonnetz diamond, the pitch roll and the tuning strip are the observable objects; the surrounding chrome is the housing that keeps them readable. Where its percussive sibling draws a rosette of pulses, this one draws a path through harmonic space and a history of the notes it produced. Both share one chamber, one type system and one control language, because they are two instruments in the same rack. The surface is sparser than nrum seq by geometry: a fixed 860x697 window, one drawing, six parameter rows, a tuning strip and a roll that is allowed to hold real air. That air is intentional. The roll is where the user reads the melody, so it gets the largest single region and the fewest marks inside it.
keyCharacteristics: Green chamber with a three-hue signal ramp and a single warm focus accent.
Fixed 860x697 coordinate space; the roll is the largest region and stays uncluttered.
The same job-named type scale as nrum seq, 9-14px, weight and tone carrying hierarchy.
Flat surfaces; depth from tonal layering, shadows only on overlays.
Two authored differentiators: the Tonnetz drawing and the tuning strip.

rules.name: The One Reading Rule
rules.body: At rest, a screen carries the roll in lime, the drawing in green and teal, and one primary action in focus orange. Everything else is neutral.

rules.name: The Signal Not Decor Rule
rules.body: A saturated colour encodes a note, a harmonic relationship, or a state the user can act on. Otherwise it is a bug.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: A label and its value share a row and differ in tone, not size.

rules.name: The 9px Floor Rule
rules.body: 9px is for labels inside geometry that cannot grow — the pitch ruler above all. A control label at 9px is a layout failure.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No surface inside the panel carries a shadow.

rules.name: The Solid State Rule
rules.body: A state fill is the accent at full opacity. A tint behind a label drops it below 4.5:1 in at least one theme; the tint is the defect, not the hue.

rules.name: The One Bloom Rule
rules.body: Motion has exactly one moment. Generate answers with a single accent bloom across the panel: 70ms to arrive, 450ms to leave. Nothing else in the chrome eases; state changes land on contact.

dos: Do keep saturated colour for notes, harmonic relationships and state only.
Do place controls in the fixed 860x697 space rather than adding breakpoints to the main panel.
Do use 3-4px radii, 1px low-contrast borders, and fills to indicate identity.
Do let the roll hold real air; it is read, not filled.
Do keep the tuning strip's four controls on one height and one label tone.
donts: Don't use gradients as fills, glows, or glass. The one gradient is the accent ramp that marks a selected row, parameter or tuning chip; it never appears as decoration.
Don't build a dark web dashboard: no purple, no translucent cards, no pills, no emoji labels.
Don't imitate a generic DAW: no brushed metal, no knobs, no tabbed preferences, no stock widget styling.
Don't build a sci-fi HUD: no scanlines, no neon wireframes, no hex grids, no idle telemetry.
Don't raise functional labels above 11px to create hierarchy; use weight and tone, and if that fails the layout is wrong.
